target.name: Steam PreyDll.dll and PreyVR source 5efd7c8f75923eec0f2553590d302e82743a2b37 with pinned takeover source edits

question: Can the near-FOV override be ordered after the renderer latch using a verified receiver, rather than assumed game/render-thread ordering?
claim: RT_BeginFrame writes the near-FOV cvar to renderer+0x95B4 before returning. The replacement detour calls that original before applying the requested value through its gated receiver. The compiled production-callback harness proves post-latch ordering, fallback-sentinel handling, next-frame disable, isolated writes and fail-closed disarming. Separate constructor/accessor bytes establish that the R-127 receiver slot is the environment physical-world member, and its weapon builder stores callerMask OR 0x400000 at +0x64.
method: Ghidra 12.1.2 /Prey/PreyDll.dll, x64 Windows, read-only tool calls plus schema-discovered localhost HTTP GET fallback. Ghidra import hash and seven byte spans compared against installed PE using Python 3.12/pefile; production prologue/latch gates independently compared to disk. MSVC 19.50, CMake Visual Studio 18 2026: build_verify.py compiles Release and runs 31 CTest checks, including the actual NearFovOverride.cpp callback with an emulated latch. Native constructor/accessor and params producer inspected; ancestor field names retained only as leads. Reproduce with collect_static.py, verify_static.py and build_verify.py in the evidence directory; native request addresses/sizes are retained in the JSON/ASM evidence.

identity.reason: Ghidra import/disk SHA-256 agree; target is x64 and seven native byte spans plus both compiled code gates match disk; source/output hashes pinned.

instrument.reason: Native bytes, disassembly and decompilation agree; production callback compiled and executed with controlled native latch in offline harness.

control.reason: Changed native FOV each frame, disable and sentinel controls; wrong slot, unreadable receiver/code, nonfinite value and mismatched opcode/displacement controls exercise refusal/disarm.

scene.reason: Static and offline test work; no game process used.

restore.reason: Persistent version-controlled source edits; no game memory or runtime configuration mutated.

baseline.reason: Release DLL build and 31/31 offline tests passed. This baseline verdict excludes game execution and headset quality.

limits: The harness never installs a hook in Prey. Actual level-load cadence, downstream per-view FOV agreement, renderer scheduling, performance and headset acceptance remain unmeasured. Physics output writer/filter/caller ownership still require target proof; no native query is shipped. FOV readback does not identify a competing writer. This does not fix equip-time rotation capture or the common reticle-origin anchor.

do_not_repeat.approach: Infer that a game-thread Render entry follows a render-thread frame latch just from frame labels.
do_not_repeat.reason: Queued rendering requires actual ordering proof; the native frame-begin return gives a narrower verified placement.
do_not_repeat.reopen_when: Producer/consumer scheduling evidence proves the proposed alternative call order.

do_not_repeat.approach: Treat equal pre-write FOV readback as proof no other writer exists.
do_not_repeat.reason: The startup cvar and another writer may both equal the requested override.
do_not_repeat.reopen_when: Writer-specific instrumentation with positive coverage controls is available.

next_action: Runtime owner should test the gated FOV return hook through level load, zoom and disable using read-only status plus rendered evidence. Next feature build recovers authored weapon/barrel-to-wrist transforms and a coherent independent head anchor, then removes arbitrary controller-angle capture across equips. Resolve the concrete scene-query implementation/output/filter contract before collision. Queue this as an existing thread/order and receiver-provenance example for fleet review, without promoting headset acceptance.
